questions.stem: According to Eli Hinkel, why do English learners who begin studying after a certain age struggle to sound exactly like a native speaker?
options: They did not study hard enough as children.
The brain loses some ability to control mouth muscles after physical growth stops.
They lack access to good textbooks.
Native speakers refuse to help them practice.
questions.evidence: After your physical growth has stopped, the brain loses some of its ability to change the way it controls the muscles of the mouth.
questions.explanation_ko: 신체 성장이 멈춘 뒤에는 뇌가 입 근육을 조절하는 능력의 일부를 잃는다고 나와 있습니다.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT mentioned as advice for improving pronunciation?
options: Choosing one or two difficult sounds to work on
Understanding that progress can be slow
Avoiding people who claim quick fixes for accents
Watching only native-speaker movies every day
questions.evidence: Choose one or two sounds that are difficult for you to pronounce.
questions.explanation_ko: 원어민 영화만 매일 보라는 조언은 본문에 나오지 않습니다.

questions.stem: What can be inferred from the fact that Hinkel, a native Russian speaker, believes her accent helps her when teaching?
options: Having an accent makes someone unable to teach a language effectively.
An accent can even be an advantage in certain teaching situations.
Only native speakers should teach English.
Hinkel is trying to lose her Russian accent.
questions.evidence: She believes her accent helps her when she is teaching students.
questions.explanation_ko: 억양이 오히려 가르치는 데 도움이 된다고 믿는다는 내용에서, 억양이 특정 상황에서는 오히려 장점이 될 수 있음을 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.stem: Why does the author compare setting reasonable pronunciation goals to deciding to diet?
options: To suggest that setting achievable, specific goals leads to more success, as with dieting
To recommend that language learners also change their eating habits
To criticize people who go on diets
To explain the biology of muscle memory
questions.evidence: like when you decide to diet, you are more likely to have success if you set reasonable goals
questions.explanation_ko: 이 비유는 다이어트처럼 실현 가능하고 구체적인 목표를 세울 때 더 성공할 가능성이 높다는 점을 보여 주기 위한 것입니다.

questions.stem: In the passage, what does "disheartened" mean in "should not be too disheartened about their accents"?
options: proud
discouraged or upset
confused
excited
questions.evidence: English learners should not be too disheartened about their accents

blanks.sentence_ko: 원어민처럼 들리지 않는다고 해서 발음을 개선하려는 시도를 포기해야 한다는 뜻은 아니다.
학습자들은 사람들의 억양을 없애 주겠다고 주장하는 사람들에게 속아서는 안 된다고 그는 말했다.
사춘기에 이르지 않은 사람들은 뇌가 입 근육을 조절할 수 있을 만큼 충분한 근육과 뇌의 가소성을 아직 가지고 있다고 그는 말한다.
당신에게는 발전이 느릴 수 있지만, 포기하지 마세요!

key_points: Setting language-learning goals helps learners stay motivated, but unreasonable goals, like sounding exactly like a native speaker, can lead to discouragement.

According to Eli Hinkel, learners who start studying English after puberty usually cannot sound exactly like a native speaker because the brain's control over mouth muscles becomes less flexible with age.
Having an accent does not mean a person's language skills are poor, and it can even be an advantage, as Hinkel believes hers is when teaching.
Marla Yoshida recommends setting specific, reasonable pronunciation goals, such as improving one or two difficult sounds at a time, rather than trying to eliminate an accent entirely.
main_idea: Because it is naturally difficult for most adult learners to sound exactly like a native speaker, experts recommend setting reasonable, specific pronunciation goals instead of trying to eliminate an accent.
restate_sentence: Goals help guide language learners and give them reasons to continue studying a language.
